description: Configuration for the ERPNext MCP server: the master switch, the token an AI client authenticates with, the network allowlist, and one switch per tool.

fields.description: Master switch. While this is off the MCP endpoint answers 404 for everyone, whatever else is configured here. This is the fastest way to cut off an AI client: untick, save, done — no restart, no token change.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: Token an MCP client must present, as X-MCP-Token (or Authorization: Bearer where the site's OAuth layer leaves it alone). Generated by the button below; stored encrypted and never shown again, logged or returned by any tool. Treat it as read access to your entire general ledger.
fields.label: Auth Token

fields.description: When the current token was created. Rotate it if it may have leaked.
fields.label: Token Generated On
Endpoint
fields.options:
Endpoint
POST https://<your-site>/api/method/erpnext_mcp.mcp.handle

Header
X-MCP-Token: <token>

JSON-RPC 2.0 (MCP Streamable HTTP). POST only — this server sends no unsolicited messages, so there is no stream to open.

Every call, allowed or refused, is recorded in MCP Action Log.

fields.description: Comma- or newline-separated CIDR blocks allowed to reach the endpoint, checked after the token. Defaults to loopback plus private LAN ranges. An empty list denies everyone — a blank field is far more often a mistake than an intent to publish an accounting API. Add 0.0.0.0/0 only if you genuinely mean the whole internet.
fields.label: Allowed CIDRs

fields.description: On: tools run as the MCP System User below, so every document an AI created carries an owner that is obviously not a person, and every permission-checked tool (reports, attachments, comments, workflow actions) is bounded by that user's roles. Off: they run as Administrator, which works but makes MCP-authored documents indistinguishable from an admin's own. Leave this on unless you have a specific reason.
fields.label: Attribute Actions To An MCP System User

fields.description: The user tools run as, and that mutations are attributed to. Create a dedicated one (for example mcp@yourcompany.example) with only the roles the tools you enabled actually need — Accounts User is normally enough for the ledger tools; reports, attachments and workflow actions need whatever their own DocTypes require. Falls back to Administrator if left empty.
fields.label: MCP System User

fields.description: All on by default; none of these can change data. Turning one off removes it from the catalogue entirely, so a client cannot see it. Use this to keep an AI's view down to the job it is doing.
fields.label: Accounting Read Tools

fields.description: Map companies, cost centers, fiscal years and chart-of-accounts roots. The orientation call every client should make first.
fields.label: Get Company Topology

fields.description: Balance of one account as of a date, summed from GL Entry.
fields.label: Get Account Balance

fields.description: Paginated Journal Entry headers by date range, company, account and docstatus.
fields.label: Get Journal Entries

fields.description: One Journal Entry with every account line, party and reference.
fields.label: Get Journal Entry

fields.description: Bank Transactions by account, date range and status.
fields.label: List Bank Transactions

fields.description: One Bank Statement, where this ERPNext version has the doctype.
fields.label: Get Bank Statement

fields.description: Fiscal years and the companies they apply to.
fields.label: List Fiscal Years

fields.description: The chart of accounts as a nested tree.
fields.label: Get Chart Of Accounts

fields.description: Bank Transactions with money still unallocated.
fields.label: List Unreconciled Bank Transactions

fields.description: Fuzzy account lookup by number or name. Turn this off and a client must know exact docnames.
fields.label: Search Accounts

fields.description:
Every one of these is off on a fresh install and stays off until you tick it. Each call is recorded in MCP Action Log with its arguments and its docstatus change. Enable the narrowest set that does the job: create_journal_entry alone gives an AI a scratchpad in the ledger, because a draft affects no balance until submit_journal_entry — a separate switch — posts it.

Two more write tools live in the sections below: Advance Workflow (Workflow) and Create Todo (Comments & Tasks). The banner at the top of this form always lists every write tool that is currently live, wherever its switch is.
fields.label: Accounting Write Tools

fields.description: Create a DRAFT Journal Entry (docstatus 0). Cannot submit. Balances are unaffected until something else submits it.
fields.label: Create Journal Entry

fields.description: Submit an existing draft Journal Entry (0 to 1). THIS MOVES BALANCES and writes GL Entries.
fields.label: Submit Journal Entry

fields.description: Cancel a submitted Journal Entry (1 to 2), writing reversing GL Entries. Requires a reason.
fields.label: Cancel Journal Entry

fields.description: Insert a DRAFT Bank Transaction.
fields.label: Create Bank Transaction

fields.description: Attach payment vouchers to a Bank Transaction, up to its unallocated amount.
fields.label: Reconcile Bank Transaction

fields.description: Reading a site's approval structure, and — behind its own switch — acting on it. Workflow actions run through Frappe's own apply_workflow, so they respect the acting user's roles and the transition's conditions.
fields.label: Workflow

fields.description: Every Workflow definition: governed DocType, states, transitions and roles.
fields.label: List Workflows

fields.description: Where one document sits in its workflow and which transitions lead out of that state.
fields.label: Get Workflow State

fields.description: Documents parked in a state that still has an action available, optionally narrowed to one user's roles.
fields.label: List Pending Approvals

fields.description: Which workflow actions the acting MCP user can take on a document right now.
fields.label: List Available Actions

fields.description: WRITE. Take a workflow action on a document via Frappe's apply_workflow. Moves state and can submit or cancel the document, exactly as the Desk button does.
fields.label: Advance Workflow

fields.description: A site's saved reports are usually the most trustworthy answer to an accounting question, because somebody who knew the schema already wrote them. run_report enforces the acting user's permission on the report's DocType, so it can reach figures the raw read tools cannot — and is bounded by the roles you gave the MCP System User.
fields.label: Reports

fields.description: Every saved Report, its ref_doctype and its report_type.
fields.label: List Reports

fields.description: Run a Query, Script or Report Builder report and return its rows. Respects the acting user's permission on the report's DocType. Reports often expose figures the individual read tools do not.
fields.label: Run Report

fields.description: Both tools check read permission on the parent document before returning anything, and treat an unattached private file as its owner's. Turn Get Attachment Content off if files on this site hold anything an AI client should never read.
fields.label: Attachments

fields.description: Files attached to a document. Checks read permission on that document.
fields.label: List Attachments

fields.description: Base64 content of one attachment, size-capped. Honours private-file permissions. Turn this off if attachments on this site hold anything an AI client should not read.
fields.label: Get Attachment Content

fields.description: The human layer: what people said about a document, and what is on somebody's list. List Comments checks read permission on the document. Create Todo writes.
fields.label: Comments & Tasks

fields.description: The comment and activity thread on a document. Checks read permission on that document.
fields.label: List Comments

fields.description: ToDo rows assigned to a user.
fields.label: List Assigned Todos

fields.description: WRITE. Assign a ToDo to a user. Touches no ledger, but it does put an item in somebody's queue and notify them.
fields.label: Create Todo

fields.description: Only usable where the Frappe HR (hrms) app is installed — on a site without it these tools are not advertised at all, whatever these switches say. Employee, attendance and leave data is personal information; enable deliberately.
fields.label: HR

fields.description: Employee records with department, designation and status.
fields.label: List Employees

fields.description: Per-employee counts of Present / Absent / Half Day / On Leave over a date range.
fields.label: Get Attendance Summary

fields.description: Remaining leave per type for one employee, computed by HR's own balance function.
fields.label: Get Leave Balance

fields.description: Order books and receivables ageing, from ERPNext's Selling, Buying and Accounts modules.
fields.label: Sales & Purchasing

fields.description: Sales Order headers with totals and delivery progress.
fields.label: List Sales Orders

fields.description: Submitted Sales Invoices still owed, with ageing buckets.
fields.label: Get Outstanding Invoices

fields.description: Purchase Order headers with totals and receipt progress.
fields.label: List Purchase Orders

fields.description: Site customisation, for a developer debugging their own instance. Client Script bodies are truncated to 500 characters.
fields.label: Meta

fields.description: Custom Fields on this site, in form order. For debugging why a field is not appearing.
fields.label: List Custom Fields

fields.description: Client Scripts with a truncated preview of each body.
fields.label: List Client Scripts

fields.description:
Structured artefacts for somebody who has to sign something off — each carries its own provenance and its own anomaly flags, and an ERROR flag means the numbers do not internally agree. All read-only: nothing is stored, emailed or filed.

The first two switches are the MCP tools; the rest are the individual packet types, each gated separately so you can expose a reconciliation packet without exposing a payroll one.
fields.label: Compliance Packets

fields.description: Which packet types this site can produce, and the filters each takes. Discovery only.
fields.label: List Compliance Packets

fields.description: Build a packet and return it inline. Nothing is stored, emailed or filed. Reads only what the packet needs.
fields.label: Generate Compliance Packet

fields.description: One account, one period: opening and closing balances, every Journal Entry that touched it, the drafts that would change it, the cancellations a balance query cannot see, and a check that the arithmetic closes.
fields.label: Reconciliation Packet

fields.description: A year for an outside CPA: trial balance, income statement, balance sheet, twenty largest entries, intercompany activity, document counts, and a check that the accounting identity holds.
fields.label: Fiscal Year Audit Packet
